comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C60-C63, C86-C87. Both evaluations affirm the methodological advance as supported, with peer reviewers explicitly confirming it as 'carefully validated' and a 'valuable technical advance.' Both recognize the three-component system (live imaging, in situ staining, cell tracking) as successfully demonstrated.

Perfect agreement on claims C23-C25. Both evaluations support that apoptosis is a feature of normal regeneration with appropriate controls ruling out photodamage. Peer reviewers accept these observations as part of the convincing overall characterization.

Perfect agreement on claims C56-C58. Both evaluations support the reported survival and success rates (18/21 animals survive, 30/37 legs regenerate normally). Peer reviewers confirm the methodology is rigorous and the technical feasibility is solid.

Perfect agreement on claims C112-C114. Both evaluations support the backtracking software enhancement as a useful contribution. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as part of the complementary tools employed for analysis.

Strong agreement on claims C28-C29, C115-C119 regarding imaging optimization. Both evaluations support the systematic optimization study balancing detection, linking, and proofreading effort. Peer reviewers confirm the methodology is rigorous and clearly documented, with explicit acknowledgment of the optimization work.

Strong agreement on claims C36-C40 regarding HCR adaptation. Both evaluations support this as a significant methodological advance enabling retrospective cell fate determination. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm successful implementation of HCR in situ hybridization in Parhyale.

Agreement on claims C26-C27, C48 regarding depth-dependent tracking limitations. Both evaluations support this characterization. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge tracking was restricted to upper 30 µm tissue layer without disputing the findings. OpenEval additionally includes mechanistic explanation (C107-C108).

Agreement on claims C43-C44 regarding spineless lineage analysis. Both evaluations support this as proof-of-principle demonstration. However, peer reviewers note 'biological insights from the cell lineage and molecular mapping are still limited,' indicating acceptance of results but recognition of preliminary nature.

Agreement on claims C51-C53 regarding light-sheet microscopy limitations. Both evaluations support the authors' reasoning for not using light-sheet due to mounting incompatibility. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this limitation and accept the current approach as justified.

Agreement on regeneration phase characterization (C4-C17 overlap). Both evaluations support the three-phase description. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm authors 'defined three distinct phases' based on cellular and morphological features. OpenEval covers broader temporal characterization (C1-C22) while peer review focuses on phase definitions.

Agreement on timing and variation claims C18-C22. Both evaluations support the temporal characterization and quantification of regeneration speed variation. Peer reviewers accept complete imaging spanning several days, though note 'much of the benchmarking remains qualitative.'

Agreement on claim C30 regarding deconvolution/denoising. Both evaluations support this negative finding as part of systematic optimization. Peer reviewers do not dispute it, accepting it as part of rigorous methodology.

Partial overlap on claims C45-C47. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on demonstrated capabilities. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging potential but noting 'biological insights are still limited' and 'benchmarking remains qualitative.' Both recognize promise but peer review emphasizes limitations more strongly.

Agreement on UNCERTAIN evaluation for claims C64, C90 regarding future comprehensive lineage mapping potential. Both recognize this as forward-looking with significant additional work required. Peer reviewers note 'methodology offers significant potential' but 'biological insights are still limited.'

OpenEval evaluates claims C54-C55 regarding current limitation requiring post-hoc identification as SUPPORTED. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers generally acknowledge the HCR approach as a practical solution.
